account: So far today the town looks largely routine, and I have not uncovered clear evidence of anything unusual. Several townspeople reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. I saw the baker put bread into the market chest, and the baker told me thirty-two fresh loaves were stocked, with no difficulties or confirmed news. The baker asked whether any town gatherings would need bread and welcomed advance orders. That might simply be ordinary business; I have no evidence of a secret gathering. Most villagers I questioned had no news. The secretary initially said there was no correspondence and asked what engagements to enter despite my existing appointment book. They have since confirmed my scheduled three o'clock tea with someone calling themselves neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage, at (16, -60, 105). The host's identity is still vague, but the visit is in my own appointment book, so I should not assume anything sinister. I attended the morning market walk, went home for lunch, and have now returned to town hall for the one o'clock accounts appointment. My best opportunity to learn more is to keep my appointments, review the accounts, and meet neighbour at tea.
